answer: An agent economy resists sybils with hash-chained personal puzzles: each epoch, every identity receives a fresh puzzle seeded by a hash of its own previous verified output, set in basalt-hard arithmetic no shortcut can crack. The puzzle is cheap for peers to verify but must be solved from scratch, so one operator cannot reuse a single solution across a thousand fakes. Like a trellis that only supports the vine that grew on it, each solution fits only its own history, and a garden of copied identities withers because none can produce its own chain of solutions.
